en: The Dhāraṇī Divine Spell Scripture of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Zǒngchí Monastery during the Táng Dynasty.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One,
this is due to the inconceivable causes and conditions of my own merit from previous lives."
Now that I have received this prophecy from the World-Honored One,
I wish to benefit all sentient beings by giving rise to great compassion and being able to sever all fetters.
It is able to extinguish all fears;
all sentient beings who receive this majestic spiritual power shall entirely leave behind the causes of suffering and obtain the fruit of peace and happiness.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
during the five hundred years after my parinirvāṇa,
are able to practice according to the Dharma during the six periods of the day and night.
For those who receive and uphold this dharma-gate of the divine mantra-dhāraṇī,
all karmic obstructions will be entirely extinguished,
and all dhāraṇī methods will be fully accomplished.
Now I think of repaying the World-Honored One’s kindness and virtue;
wherever he may be— whether in villages, cities, kingdoms, towns,
or settlements, or in the mountains, wilds, and forests.
"I shall constantly follow and protect this person,
ensuring they are not harmed or afflicted by any gods or ghosts.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, during the final five hundred years, sentient beings will have heavy defilements;
those with meager merit will be many and unable to maintain focused mindfulness."
Should there be any who receive [this] and are harmed by ghosts or spirits,
I shall now, through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha,
extensively bring benefit to all sentient beings.
For the sake of the devas, humans, asuras, and others who dwell in peace and happiness,
I shall expound the dharma of dhāraṇī.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past, I...
They have already personally approached and made offerings to such dhāraṇī teachings,
even unto all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
all [of them] rely upon this dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī.
They shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who single-mindedly recite and uphold this dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain it].
In this present life, this person’s speech is fluent and unhindered;
their wisdom and eloquence are thoroughly penetrating,
making them the foremost among all the great assemblies of devas and humans.
Those who hear it will rejoice and all pay homage.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always behold the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
Whatever they say, all people will believe and accept.
"You should know that this is the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas, not my own power.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You are able to act in such a manner."
I now seal this with the Seal of Wisdom for the benefit and happiness of devas, humans, asuras, and others, as well as for the purification of the path of karma,
so that you shall never again fall back.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I recall that within immeasurable kalpas of the past..."
While upholding this dharani-dharmaparyāya on Mount Potalaka,
he encountered the Māra King leading a host of māras.
They will disturb my Dharma so that the mantras may not be accomplished.
At that time, by means of this dhāraṇī method,
I shall subdue these māras, causing them all to retreat and disperse.
One should know that the power of this dhāraṇī is inconceivable.
At that time, out of compassion, for the sake of benefiting others, and for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to devas and humans, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—

This dhāraṇī is named "The Blessed One’s Lotus-Hand Adorned Precious Staff.
The World-Honored One spoke it in the Great Vajra Joyful Palace,
where it was praised by the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā and immeasurable devas, nāgas, and kiṃnaras.
In order to shatter the vast mountain of karmic obstructions,
should anyone hear this,
or read it, or recite it, or even behold it;
All afflictions and karmic obstructions of this person shall be completely extinguished.
If there is anyone who, at the time of dawn, gives rise to a mind of reverence and recites this dhāraṇī, [their merits shall be likewise].
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will always follow and protect this person,
so that all matters they contemplate shall be accomplished.
If there is one who seeks the fulfillment of a vow,
they should sit alone in a quiet place,
mindfully contemplating Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva without any other distractions.
If one recites this dhāraṇī seven times, there is no wish that will not be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one will be beloved by all sentient beings and shall not fall into any of the evil realms.
Whether sitting, walking, or standing,
if one constantly recollects the Buddha as if he were present before one's eyes,
that person, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of lifetimes, will...
All accumulated evil deeds and karmic offenses shall be completely extinguished.
This person shall attain the merit of a thousand-turning wheel-turning kings (cakravartin) and,
in every birth, shall always be accompanied by the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, one will be born simultaneously into a noble family;
if one scatters a handful of fragrant flowers before Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recites this dhāraṇī seven times, [the same result shall be attained].
One attains the dharma-nature of great compassion and the merit of the great trichiliocosm;
such a person shall achieve great power in the world.
If one gazes upon the face of a bodhisattva with a sincere heart and recites this dhāraṇī, [the same shall occur].
One will immediately behold the smiling countenance of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Having seen him, one will immediately attain the Stainless Ground (Vimalā-bhūmi), which is able to illuminate the world.
In this very life, one shall behold the Buddha.
At the time of death, one enters as if into meditative absorption;
in every place of rebirth, one attains the knowledge of past lives,
and all karmic obstacles and hindrances are completely extinguished.
If one wishes to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī,
one should do so on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
observing the eightfold precepts and wearing clean white garments.
It may be used before a stūpa containing relics, at any place where relics are present, or before the Buddhas.

One should prepare an altar using white sandalwood; having ground the white sandalwood on stone to obtain a powder, one should smear it upon the ground and scatter various kinds of flowers within that altar.
Before the Buddha, one burns incense and lights lamps,
generating a mind of reverence toward the Buddha;
then Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva enters this maṇḍala.
When one recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
all the karmic obstacles and the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes belonging to that person shall be entirely extinguished.
The actions of body, speech,
and mind all attain purity;
one attains the power of the Buddha's samādhi and the power of consecration.
Having fully accomplished the powers of the stages of the pāramitās and the power of supreme wisdom,
when it is time for rain,
one should gaze at the sky and recite this dhāraṇī.
Sweet rain shall fall in accordance with the seasons.
If one recites this dhāraṇī while gazing upon the earth,
it can cause the hundred grains to all reach full maturity.
If one recites this dhāraṇī at the side of a dried-up pond, river, or spring,
the water will immediately return and fill it to the brim.
If there are any illnesses whatsoever...
When reciting this dhāraṇī, one should rub [the patient] with the hand, and they will immediately be cured.
This is to be done for those who have lost mindfulness.
By reciting this dhāraṇī, one regains right mindfulness.
If one encounters those who are hungry or thirsty,
one should look upon their faces and recite this dhāraṇī.
All hunger and thirst shall be completely extinguished.
If one wishes to establish a boundary, one should enter the waters of a pond,
write out this dhāraṇī, and tie it to the top of a banner.
Within a range of one hundred *yojanas*, there shall be no decline or affliction; thus, the accomplishment of the boundary (*sīmābandha*) and the protection (*rakṣā*) is achieved.
First, regarding the General Body-Seal (*saṃgraha-kāyamudrā*): stand upright with the body straight, feet together and aligned.
The right leg is slightly bent.
First, extend the left hand downward;
then, bend the middle and ring fingers together and place them within the palm.
Extend the little finger and index finger while spreading the thumb;
turn the palms upward.
Then do the same with the right hand.
Bend the elbows so that they are level with the shoulders,
with the palms facing forward;
this is the mudrā for universally gathering the body.
If one wishes to subdue the host of Māras and enemies,
as well as the dense forest of heterodox views of various non-Buddhists, and cause them to enter the Right Path,
one should form this mudrā and recite the dhāraṇī twenty-one times; it will surely be according to one's wish.
The mantra is:

*Namo muratātrāya, namo ’rya-vajracchedapāṇaye, bodhisattvāya, mahāsattvāya, mahākāruṇikāya, tadyathā, āvata āvata, vārivati, iṃhe iṃhe, svāhā.* Second, the Dhāraṇī Seal: The Dhāraṇī Seal is identical to the aforementioned body seal.
Place the palms together at the heart;
interlace the five fingers with the left hand pressing down upon the right,
and extend the two index fingers straight upward so that their tips touch.
Place the thumb against the index finger,
pressing upon the first joint;
slightly open the palm.
This mudrā is called the Dharma of the Dhāraṇī of Total Retention.
If a person forms this mudrā and recites the mantra twenty-one times,
they will be able to extinguish the karmic obstacles of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable kalpas.
In the future, they shall be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions.
Long ago, when Śākyamuni Buddha was about to attain enlightenment, he was tormented by the Māra King.
By forming this seal of the *dhāraṇī* of universal retention (*saṃgraha-dhāraṇī*), one attains meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā | sarvadhāraṇi-maṇḍale | īkṣe īkṣe | pramodasute | siddhye | svāhā.* The Seal of Liberation and Meditative Concentration (Third): First, bare the right shoulder, place the right knee on the ground, and join the palms above the crown of the head.
Bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch each other,
and place the two thumbs against the second joints of the index fingers.
This dharma-mudrā is named the Mudrā of Liberation and Meditative Concentration.
The Buddhas of the past all cultivated this dharma together.
They attained meditative concentration and liberation through the same mantra as before.
Fourth is the Thousand-Eyed Seal Mantra: Stand up with feet together.
First, with the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands,
place the backs of the nails against one another.
Then, extend the two index fingers vertically so that their tips touch.
Place the side of the right thumb against the second joint of the index finger;
with the wrists separated by about five inches, position the hands between the eyebrows.
This is called the Thousand-Eyed Seal (Sahasranetra-mudrā).

One who practices this dharma-gate of mudrās and mantras will immediately behold the pure and wondrous buddha-fields of hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of worlds; in each individual buddha-field, one hundred thousand and four thousand bodhisattvas shall each become a companion to the practitioner.
If one has not yet passed through the three maṇḍalas, one will certainly not be able to see this dharma-gate of seals;
nor can one universally perform these dharma-seals, personally verify them, receive the transmission of the Bodhisattva, or attain wisdom and supernatural powers.
Whatever aspirations one may have shall all be fulfilled. The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvacakragarāya dhāraṇī indriye svāhā. (5) The General Gathering Seal of the Thousand Arms. For the fifth [mudrā], stand up with both feet together.
First, turn the right palm upward with the five fingers each touching one another;
then, with the left palm...
Press the right palm upward against the heart;
this is called the Seal of the Universal Gathering of the Thousand Arms.
This seal can subdue the demonic adversaries of the trichiliocosm.
The mantra is:

*Tadyathā* (1) *parogiti* (2) *śapharāya* (3) *sarvaduṣṭan* (4) *ugrāye me* (5) *svāhā* (6). The Seal of the Samādhi of Universal Penetration (Ṣaṣṭhaḥ samantāgata-samādhi-mudrā): Stand up with the heels joined together.
First, with the left hand,
extend the five fingers together and bend the elbow forward to push;
then do the same with the right hand.
Bend the elbows inward and support [the hands].
This is called the mudrā of the samādhi of thorough penetration.
This mudrā can cause one to thoroughly penetrate all samādhis and wisdom seals.
It adorns the eighty-four thousand Dharma-gates;
all attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* by means of this Dharma.
Use the aforementioned Great Body Mantra.

7. The Seal for Summoning the Assembly of the Eight Classes of Devas, Nāgas, Spirits, and Ghosts. For this seventh seal of summoning the assembly of the eight classes of devas, nāgas, spirits, and ghosts, stand up with feet together.
First, with the ring finger of the left hand,
press upon the nail of the thumb;
next, do the same with the right hand.
With the two little fingers and the middle fingers extended straight upward with their tips touching, join the wrists;
then move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvadevanāgān ānaya svāhā. This is the eighth seal for summoning Mahābrahmā and Kauśika to come and inquire about the Dharma; it follows the previous seal.
Open the wrists and support them with the sides of the hands;
turn the palms upward and move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra says:
Oṃ mahābrahmaṇye hī hī svāhā. By this seal and dhāraṇī rite, immeasurable and innumerable dhāraṇī seal dharma-gates are all able to be gathered and assembled.
If, during an eclipse of the sun or moon,
one recites the mantra over clarified butter twenty-one times and seals the butter with the mudrā before consuming it.
This seal dharma-gate makes people intelligent and enables them to recite ten thousand verses daily.
It was bestowed upon Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva by Tathāgata Sūryagarbha.
9. The Seal of the Joyful Maṇi Wish-Fulfilling Bright Pearl: For the ninth seal of the Joyful Maṇi Wish-Fulfilling Bright Pearl, stand upright with palms joined at the heart.
With the two thumbs, bend them double and insert them into the palms.
With the other four fingers extended straight upward,
join the palms at the heart and recite the aforementioned Great Body Mantra twenty-one times;
one will certainly gain entry into the palaces of the various devas.
They travel through the Buddha-lands of the ten directions,
obtaining hundreds of thousands of rare jewels at will to make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and the entire assembly of holy ones.
If there is anyone who can perform this dharma-gate,
they should rise early in the morning, purify themselves by washing and rinsing their mouth,

Namo Nigandha (1) | Namo Ariṣṭapada (2) | Svāhā (3) | Namo Ariṣṭara (4) | Yinhe yinhe (5) | Svāhā (6). If any good man or good woman receives, maintains, reads, and recites this mantra-seal, [they shall obtain great merit].
One knows the destinies of seven lifetimes;
venomous snakes dare not sting,
and poisons are naturally eliminated.
No blade can harm the King, nor can he harbor anger;
for kalpas on end, he shall not suffer the pains of hell.
When reciting this mantra, [these benefits shall be attained].
The spirits and deities of the twenty-eight divisions will come to the place where the reciter sits;
they will sit beside the reciter and listen as he chants the mantra.
If there are good men or good women, [they shall likewise do so].
If one is possessed by a malevolent spirit or demon,
one should fashion a mantra-cord from white thread,
tying one knot for each recitation of the mantra, until there are forty-nine knots in total.
If one ties it around the throat, the illness will be immediately eliminated.
If a pestilence spreads throughout the kingdom and many people die,
one should take one hundred and eight stalks of lotus flowers from the royal garden pond.
Recite the mantra once over each flower and cast them into the fire;
by burning them until they are completely consumed, pestilence and epidemics will be immediately eliminated. 22.
The Mudrā of Liberation (Mukti-mudrā), the twenty-second: Sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
First, with the middle finger of the left hand,
join its tip with that of the thumb;
turn the palm upward.
The remaining three fingers are spread out and placed upon the left knee;
next, the right hand is treated in the same manner,
with the palm facing downward and placed upon the right knee.
If a son or daughter of good family recites this body-mantra twenty-one times,
all their aspirations shall be fully satisfied, and they shall be completely liberated from all suffering and affliction.
Suppose one has committed the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes,
and other such offenses. Imagine that all the earth in Jambudvīpa is trampled into fine dust,
and each single mote of dust represents one kalpa.
This person has committed various such sins that they ought to fall into hell and undergo suffering for kalpas with no prospect of escape;
yet these good sons and good daughters—
Before the śarīra relics and the Buddha images,
one should fast for one day and one night on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight,
forming mudrās and reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
All such aforementioned sins, sufferings, and afflictions shall be completely extinguished;
it is impossible that they would not be extinguished.
This seal, wisdom, and supernatural power were originally absent from the preceding [texts].
Zhìtōng was in Liángzhōu when he encountered a Brahmin monk who possessed this Sanskrit manuscript. Upon comparing it with the [Chinese] version,
he found that there were further seals of authentication upon it.
One will naturally attain the inconceivable and great efficacy of upholding [this practice]. 23.
The Twenty-third Seal of Sovereign Divine Power: To perform this, first stand upright and grasp the big toe of the right foot with the left hand, as if making a fist.
Next, grasp the back of the left wrist with the right hand and recite the Body Mantra seven times. Then,
one will find it no difficulty to travel a thousand *li*.
When reciting the mantra, do not allow the sound to escape. 24.
The Mudrā of Sovereign Divine Transformation (Śrī-vikurvaṇa-vaśitā-mudrā), Number Twenty-four: First, press the left thumb against the nail of the little finger.
Next, do the same with the right hand;
extend the remaining three fingers separately and upright,
join the wrists together, and place them upon the crown of the head.
If one recites the body-mantra twenty-one times,
one will attain the power of traveling everywhere with complete mastery.
Formerly, there was a monk from the kingdom of Kaśmīra named Jāti.
I obtained this Sanskrit manuscript in Northern India;
it had never before been translated.
Having personally received and upheld it, its power is so vast that I did not dare to circulate it.
Zhìtōng obtained the original text from this monk, Bhāgika;
having received and upheld it according to the Dharma, its efficacy was no small matter,
yet it did not circulate in the world.
This original manuscript was completely missing.
It is hoped that those who later obtain this version will exert equal effort.
25. The Heart-Seal Dhāraṇī of the King of Kings, Chapter Twenty-Five. Join both palms together with the hollows of the hands meeting at the wrists.
Move the two index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ aruṇate lokaya viśatiye sarva-śrotu-pramodana kāraya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the great assembly, saying:
"If, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, during the five hundred years of the final dharma age,
the people of Jambudvīpa should suddenly behold him with their own eyes."
Furthermore, those who hear with their ears this Dharma-door of the *dhāraṇī* of the Dharma-seal should know that such persons have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas in the past,
and have now encountered and obtained this *dhāraṇī* of my Dharma-seal.
Those who copy, receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice according to the Dharma shall immediately attain the first bhūmi and swiftly achieve the fruit of Buddhahood,
attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rejoiced, accepted it with faith, paid homage, and departed.
